posts.title: Geta for the evening bath walk
posts.excerpt: The street has seven public baths. Here is a loop that visits three and crosses the little bridge twice.
posts.content:
Start at the bath by the station, follow the stream uphill and cross the arched bridge to the old stone bath. Low rounded geta are the best on the wet tiles.

Come back on the other bank under the willows. After dark the street is quiet enough to hear every step: karan, koron.

posts.title: Geta in the rain
posts.excerpt: Wooden soles lift you above the puddles; a toe cover keeps the straps dry.
posts.content:
Geta were made for wet streets. Taller teeth keep the hem clear, and paulownia dries quickly once you are home.

Ask for a toe cover at the counter; it slips over the front of the sole and comes off in a second.

posts.title: How we set a strap
posts.excerpt: Ten minutes at the counter decide whether a pair feels good for years.
posts.content:
You stand on the sole, and we pull the strap through three holes and knot it underneath. The front should hold the toes loosely; the heel can hang a finger over the back.

After a week of walking the cloth settles. Bring the pair back and we tighten it for free, as many times as you like.
